note: Groups by family: f2 on machine 0, f1 then f0 on machine 1, with maintenance about every 5 jobs. Main risk: the heavy f0 jobs (13, 16, 8, 20) land late on machine 1.
Pure WSPT (weight/duration) alternating between machines, ignoring families. Main risk: many setups and idle time waiting for late releases (13, 16), while early-due jobs 4, 22 and 0 slip.
Family batching with no maintenance at all. Main risk: wear builds to about 1.9x by the end of each machine and blows up tail lateness.
EDD (earliest due date) with maintenance every 4-5 jobs, keeping families together where possible. Main risk: EDD ignores weights, and the mixed families add setups.
Same family batching but with frequent maintenance (every 3 jobs). Main risk: 4 maintenances per machine cost 40 time units, more than the wear they save.
Moves the heavy f0 jobs earlier on machine 1 and pushes low-weight f1 jobs (18, 24, 27) to the end. Main risk: f1 jobs 7 and 6 (w=4) come out late.
Strict family split: all f2 on machine 0, f1 and f0 on machine 1. Main risk: imbalanced load (100 vs 140 nominal units) drives up lateness on machine 1.
Naive baseline: even-numbered jobs on machine 0, odd on machine 1, in number order, no maintenance. Main risk: constant setups, wear and ignored due dates.
